chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
I and Ibrahim ibn Hashim were in some of the graveyards when he came to a grave, sat facing the Qiblah, then placed his hand on the grave and recited seven times: 'Inna anzalnahu'.

Then he said: The owner of the grave, who is Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', narrated to me that whoever visits the grave of a believer and recites at it seven times 'Inna anzalnahu', Allah will forgive him and the owner of the grave.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: Indeed, We sent it down (opening of Surah Al-Qadr)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْقَبْرِ: The owner of the grave (the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Qadr at a believer's grave?
ai.summary: This tradition from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the spiritual efficacy of visiting graves (*ziyarat*) by reciting the opening verse of Surah Al-Qadr seven times while facing the Qiblah. The practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the intercessory merit of the deceased and the tangible spiritual rewards for the living, linking the commemoration of the Night of Decree with the forgiveness of sins for both parties.
